findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the existing conflict machinery (`_diff_fields` conflict_sink / a713-a118 baseline arbitration + `_apply_outbound_conflict` / `conflict_bug_filing`) as the reuse target for the LWW conflict signal, confirming no new parallel conflict emitter is added.
evidence: Existing machinery: `outbound_fields._diff_fields` (:354) already computes local-wins with a `conflict_sink` populated when `local != baseline AND jira != baseline` (bug a713; docstring :371-373), using the per-binding `get_baseline` as arbitration ancestor (:393-400).
Downstream conflict emission already exists: `apply_outbound._apply_outbound_conflict`, `run_differs._emit_outbound_field_alerts` (conflict_sink), and `conflict_bug_filing.file_conflict_bug_ticket`.
Plan's AC5 frames a '799/799 detected' conflict invariant and `test_concurrent_conflict_detected` as new, but does not reference conflict_sink/a713/a118 as the mechanism being reused.
findings.finding: The plan describes 'three-way baseline diff + LWW arbitration' and 'emit a detectable conflict signal' as this story's approach without naming the existing both-sides-conflict machinery it should reuse, risking a re-implementation of functionality already present.
findings.location: Approach (echo-safety + concurrency); Scope: 'the existing description differ / compare path — three-way baseline diff + LWW arbitration'
scenarios: Author builds a fresh LWW+conflict emitter in reconcile_check.py rather than routing the description field through the existing _diff_fields conflict_sink path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the conflict mechanism concretely: name the detectable-signal sink (log token / ticket comment / store field) AND state how the losing side's value is preserved or recoverable, so 'never silently destroyed' is a real guarantee rather than an LWW overwrite plus a log line.
evidence: Plan: 'apply last-write-wins to pick the winner but always emit a detectable conflict signal so nothing is silently lost'
Existing outbound_fields.py has direction-suppression (local==prev → suppress) but no conflict emission — search for 'conflict' returns no matches
LWW by construction overwrites the loser; a signal is orthogonal to preserving the loser's value
findings.finding: The LWW conflict handling names no mechanism for how the losing side is preserved; 'emit a detectable conflict signal' is asserted with no named sink, and LWW overwrites the loser on the wire, so the AC 'losing side never silently destroyed' is not backed by a concrete mechanism.
findings.location: Approach (echo-safety + concurrency); AC 'A concurrent both-sides edit is detected and flagged under LWW with the losing side never silently destroyed'
scenarios: Both sides edit the body; LWW picks local, the applier overwrites the Jira-side edit, and the only 'signal' is a log line — the Jira author's text is gone with no recovery path, yet the AC claims it is 'never silently destroyed'.
